climbing_route.label: Ridge below Paul Bunyan's Stump to the Pinnacle-Pyramid saddle
climbing_route.notes: Above treeline the cairned path crosses slabs and heather benches past a couple of small tarns, then the route splits: continue up onto the ridge below Paul Bunyan's Stump and traverse below/around Pinnacle Peak to the saddle between Pinnacle and Pyramid (parties bound for Colonial Peak instead drop left onto a cedar bench into the Colonial Creek basin). East-facing snowfields and a notch/traverse just below the summit ridge hold snow well into summer, so carry an ice axe (crampons in early season) even in July-August. Route-finding is the genuine crux of the day, and the notch below the summit ridge is one of the places parties most often go off-route.

climbing_route.label: Final stretch to the summit
climbing_route.notes: From the Pinnacle-Pyramid saddle the final stretch to the summit is an easy, non-technical hike/scramble over talus and lingering snow patches. The summit itself is broad and nearly flat.

climbing_route.label: SE slopes/gully to the east ridge notch
climbing_route.notes: From the talus/scree basin at 5,500-5,700 ft directly below Reynolds Peak's southeast face, ascend the scree, talus, and (seasonally) snow of the SE slopes/gully to a saddle/notch on the peak's east ridge. This basin and the gully above it hold snow well into summer in most years, so carry an ice axe and traction in early season even on an otherwise dry-looking late-summer day.

climbing_route.label: Summit rocks from the notch
climbing_route.notes: A short, exposed class 2-3 scramble, occasionally reported as harder (class 3-4) depending on snow coverage, up sound granite summit rocks to the 8,517 ft high point.

climbing_route.label: Out of Leroy Basin to the 7,200-7,800 ft shoulder
climbing_route.notes: From camp in Leroy Basin (about 6,100 ft), aim for the broad southwest slope: two parallel lines lead out of the basin - a rock gully straight up to the lower southwest slope, or a gentler ridge to its right - and they merge in a flat shoulder around 7,200-7,800 ft where the wide, rocky southwest slope proper begins. Some parties climb to the base of cliffs near 7,200 ft then cut right to the 7,800 ft bench, described as the easiest line. A lingering snow gully in the entry couloir in early season may require an ice axe.

climbing_route.label: Southwest slope proper
climbing_route.notes: An extended ascent of loose talus and scree - boulder-hop and pick the cleanest line, favoring rock over scree where possible - trending slightly left up the slope toward the summit rocks, with a few short steeper steps that can be passed on either side without real difficulty. Loose talus/scree underfoot the entire upper mountain, exposed ridge/slope travel above treeline with no shelter from weather, and route-finding that gets harder in poor visibility since there is no single defined trail above Leroy Basin.

climbing_route.label: Ravine below the summit spires to the true summit block
climbing_route.notes: Near the top, cross a shallow ravine below the summit spires and follow a faint climbers' trail up to the left-most (true) summit block at 9,078 ft.

climbing_route.label: Weden Pass traverse and northeast ridge
climbing_route.notes: From Weden Pass (5,120 ft), traverse southwest toward the notch on the north side of Sheep Gap's main summit, dropping to around 4,900 ft on the traverse, then climb the northeast ridge toward the middle/main summit. Class 2-3 talus and heather. The talus traverses between Weden Pass and the summit are exposed and sometimes wet; a helmet is recommended.

climbing_route.label: Final summit block
climbing_route.notes: The final summit block turns into sustained class 3-4 rock and brush with one short step requiring a rope belay. Loose rock and brush on the class 3/4 sections are the named hazard here.

climbing_route.label: East ridge of Skyline/Heather Ridge
climbing_route.notes: Beyond the boulder garden, gain the undulating east ridge of the horseshoe-shaped Skyline/Heather Ridge and follow it west, traversing beneath a band of rocky outcrops before the final push to Sky Mountain's summit block. The ridge re-gains elevation repeatedly. A faint climbers' path is reported to persist most of the way to the summit when snow-free. The exposed south-facing slopes below the ridge are a known avalanche path - several fatal slides have occurred here in winter - so this route is best done in summer/early autumn.

climbing_route.label: False sub-summit to the true summit
climbing_route.notes: The undulating ridge tops out at a lower, rockier sub-summit that most parties mistake for the true summit; reaching the actual high point requires a steep traverse on the south side of that outcrop before a short final climb.

climbing_route.label: Colonial Glacier to the Colonial-Neve col
climbing_route.notes: From the moraine camp at the base of the Colonial Glacier (~5,900-6,100 ft), rope up for glacier travel - crevasses present - and climb the Colonial Glacier south to the broad Colonial-Neve col (~6,800-6,900 ft), where a stream/waterfall makes a second good camp and water source.

climbing_route.label: Neve Glacier crossing
climbing_route.notes: Descend about 200 ft from the col onto the Neve Glacier and cross it - a moderate, usually well-tracked but crevassed glacier crossing requiring a rope - to the rocks just below Snowfield's summit pyramid on its northwest side.

climbing_route.label: Long gully to the notch below the summit
climbing_route.notes: From the rocks on the northwest side, a long class 3 gully leads to a notch below the true summit.

climbing_route.label: Notch traverse to the summit
climbing_route.notes: The final short traverse/scramble across the notch to the south side and up to the summit (8,351 ft) is exposed class 3, with one move occasionally rated low class 4.

climbing_route.label: West ridge/west slope from Sperry Saddle
climbing_route.notes: From the saddle/notch between Vesper and Sperry Peaks it is off-trail scrambling up Sperry's west ridge/west slope - loose, often wet dirt and heather with class 3 rock steps, including some brushy, tree-assisted moves in the final push to the summit block - to the 6,120 ft summit. No water beyond Vesper Lake, so top off before leaving the lake.

wa_the_temple_south_ridge.skip_reason: The approach text stops exactly at the base of the South Ridge's technical section (a final sandy ramp under an overhang above Tamarack Meadows) and describes none of the climbing above it.
